values: GNG versus deterministic Halton/PRM • 800-node budget • preview-only exact collision validation
• GNG strongly reduced component count: mean 1.70 versus 11.82; paired mean reduction 10.12 (95% bootstrap CI 9.22–11.02).
• GNG construction was slower: 1723.78 ms versus 1413.57 ms; paired difference −310.20 ms when positive is defined as favoring GNG.
• Clear-scene planning time did not differ after Holm correction: adjusted p = 0.566.
• Conditional on both methods succeeding, dynamic planning time did not differ after correction: adjusted p = 0.383 (n = 42 pairs).
• Dynamic success favored Halton/PRM: GNG 42/50 versus Halton/PRM 50/50; paired risk difference −16.0 pp (95% CI −26.0 to −6.0), exact McNemar Holm-adjusted p = 0.0234.
• Interpretation: this fixed-scene experiment exposes a connectivity–robustness trade-off; it does not establish generalization or physical execution safety.
Background hardware/perception processes remained active; ROS benchmark traffic used domains 20–119 and method order was counterbalanced.

values: Positive paired effects favor GNG; timing comparisons use Halton/PRM − GNG. Dynamic time is conditional on joint success.
Exploratory outcomes; raw p-values are not included in the five-test primary Holm family.
Failures are retained; no seed was discarded or rerun. Exact replans demonstrate the reject-edge → graph-search loop.
Positive values favor GNG under each metric's predefined direction; blanks denote pairs excluded by joint-success conditioning.
Unmodified 100-row CSV snapshot; one row per method × seed. Use filters to inspect failures, timings, and exact replans.
Use this sheet with Raw Data and the reproducible Python analysis script to audit every reported result.
One deterministic seed, paired across GNG and Halton/PRM.
Seeds 0–49. The same seed-specific Halton start offset supplies GNG training samples and the Halton/PRM nodes.
Even seeds run GNG then Halton; odd seeds reverse the order to reduce monotonic host-load or thermal bias.
Connected components, build time, clear planning time, dynamic planning time conditional on joint success, and dynamic success.
For lower-is-better outcomes: Halton/PRM − GNG. For higher-is-better outcomes: GNG − Halton/PRM. Positive values favor GNG.
95% percentile paired bootstrap, 20,000 resamples of seed pairs; rank-biserial intervals use 10,000 paired resamples.
Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank with Pratt handling of zero differences. Rank-biserial correlation is the paired nonparametric effect size.
Exact McNemar/binomial test on discordant pairs. Effect magnitude is paired risk difference with bootstrap CI; matched odds ratio uses Haldane 0.5 correction.
Holm adjustment across the five prespecified primary tests. Secondary p-values are exploratory and unadjusted.
Failures are outcomes, not missing values. Dynamic timing is analyzed only for seeds where both methods succeed and is reported alongside success.
The benchmark publishes only synthetic JointState, typed environment graph, and preview paths in isolated ROS domains. It does not create a controller action client.
This fixed robot, target, and obstacle measures seed-level roadmap variability; it does not establish scene-level generalization or physical execution performance.
AGX hardware/perception processes remained active. This is disclosed because host contention can affect wall-clock measurements.
